title: XERODERMA PIGMENTOSUM, VARIANT TYPE
alt_titles: XERODERMA PIGMENTOSUM WITH NORMAL DNA REPAIR RATES

intro.text: A number sign (#) is used with this entry because of evidence that xeroderma pigmentosum, variant type (XPV) is caused by mutation in the gene encoding DNA polymerase eta (POLH).

checks.claim: Xeroderma pigmentosum, variant type (XPV) is caused by mutation in the gene encoding DNA polymerase eta (POLH).
checks.evidence_quote: We found that all XP-V cells examined carry mutations in their DNA polymerase eta gene.
checks.explanation: The abstract reports POLH mutations in all XP-V cells and concludes that pol eta could be the XPV gene product. The authors hedge this conclusion.

paragraphs.text: Xeroderma pigmentosum variant (XP-V) is an inherited disorder with the clinical features of xeroderma pigmentosum (XP), including an increased incidence of sunlight-induced skin cancers (Wang et al., 1991; Masutani et al., 1999). Unlike cells from XP groups A to G, XP-V cells carry out normal or nearly normal nucleotide excision repair of UV-induced DNA damage but are defective in replicating UV-damaged DNA (Masutani et al., 1999). XP-V cells are only slightly more sensitive than normal cells to the cytotoxic effect of UV radiation but are significantly more sensitive to its mutagenic effect (Wang et al., 1991).

checks.claim: Xeroderma pigmentosum variant (XP-V) is an inherited disorder with the clinical features of xeroderma pigmentosum.
checks.evidence_quote: Xeroderma pigmentosum variant (XP-V) is an inherited disorder which is associated with increased incidence of sunlight-induced skin cancers. Unlike other xeroderma pigmentosum cells
checks.explanation: The abstract calls XP-V an inherited disorder within XP but does not describe its clinical features beyond skin cancer.

checks.claim: Xeroderma pigmentosum variant includes an increased incidence of sunlight-induced skin cancers.

checks.evidence_quote: Unlike other xeroderma pigmentosum cells (belonging to groups XP-A to XP-G), XP-V cells carry out normal nucleotide-excision repair processes
checks.explanation: The abstract says 'normal' rather than 'normal or nearly normal', but the gist matches.

paragraphs.text: Cleaver et al. (1980) found that, in UV-irradiation studies of DNA repair and replication, a pigmented xerodermoid cell culture could not be told apart from the XP variant. They concluded that the term 'pigmented xerodermoid', which had been defined by mild clinical symptoms, was therefore redundant.

checks.evidence_quote: It is concluded that a pigmented xerodermoid cell culture is indistinguishable from the XP variant and the former term is therefore redundant.
checks.explanation: Abstract states the cell culture was indistinguishable from the XP variant after UV-irradiation studies of repair and replication.

checks.claim: Cleaver et al. (1980) concluded that the term 'pigmented xerodermoid', defined by mild clinical symptoms, was redundant.
checks.evidence_quote: The "pigmented xerodermoid" was previously defined on the basis of mild clinical symptoms that suggested it might be similar to but distinct from xeroderma pigmentosum (XP).
checks.explanation: Abstract defines the term by mild clinical symptoms and concludes 'the former term is therefore redundant.'

paragraphs.text: Lehmann et al. (1975) found that cells from XP patients whose excision repair of UV-induced pyrimidine dimers was completely normal (XP variants) had an abnormality in DNA synthesis after UV irradiation: the variant cells took much longer than normal cells to convert the low-molecular-weight DNA first made after UV irradiation into high-molecular-weight DNA. Caffeine strongly inhibited this slow conversion in UV-irradiated XP variant cells but had no effect in normal cells. Two excision repair-deficient XP cell lines showed intermediate effects, both in the time needed for the conversion and in the degree of caffeine inhibition.

checks.claim: Lehmann et al. (1975) found that cells from XP variant patients had completely normal excision repair of UV-induced pyrimidine dimers.
checks.evidence_quote: There is, however, one class of these patients whose cells are completely normal in this excision repair process.
checks.explanation: The abstract presents this as a known feature of this class of patients rather than a new finding of the study. The content itself matches the claim.

checks.claim: Lehmann et al. (1975) found that XP variant cells had an abnormality in DNA synthesis after UV irradiation, taking much longer than normal cells to convert low-molecular-weight DNA made after UV irradiation into high-molecular-weight DNA.
checks.evidence_quote: The time taken to convert initially low-molecular-weight DNA synthesized in UV-irradiated cells into high-molecular-weight DNA similar in size to that in untreated cells is much greater in these variants than in normal cells.
checks.explanation: The abstract states this directly, and also says the cells have an abnormality in how DNA is synthesized after UV irradiation.

checks.claim: Lehmann et al. (1975) found that caffeine strongly inhibited the conversion of low- to high-molecular-weight DNA in UV-irradiated XP variant cells.
checks.evidence_quote: Furthermore, this slow conversion of low to high-molecular-weight newly synthesized DNA is drastically inhibited by caffeine, which has no effect in normal cells.
checks.explanation: The paper's 'drastically inhibited' matches the draft's 'strongly inhibited'.

checks.claim: Lehmann et al. (1975) found that caffeine had no effect on the conversion of low- to high-molecular-weight DNA in UV-irradiated normal cells.
checks.evidence_quote: this slow conversion of low to high-molecular-weight newly synthesized DNA is drastically inhibited by caffeine, which has no effect in normal cells.
checks.explanation: The abstract states directly that caffeine had no effect in normal cells.

checks.claim: Lehmann et al. (1975) found that 2 excision repair-deficient XP cell lines showed intermediate effects in the time needed for conversion of low- to high-molecular-weight DNA and in the degree of caffeine inhibition.
checks.evidence_quote: Two cell lines from classes of xeroderma pigmentosum that are defective in excision-repair show intermediate effects, with regard to both the time taken to convert newly synthesized DNA to high molecular weight and the inhibition of this process by caffeine.
checks.explanation: The abstract states this directly, including that there were 2 cell lines.

paragraphs.text: Itoh et al. (2000) studied 2 independent Japanese families with 2 photosensitive patients identified as having XPV. Cells from the heterozygous parents showed normal unscheduled DNA synthesis, normal recovery of RNA synthesis, and normal recovery of replicative DNA synthesis, but reduced recovery of replicative DNA synthesis in the presence of 1 mM caffeine (53 +/- 8% of normal). In a colony-forming assay, heterozygote cells had normal UV survival without caffeine but slightly reduced survival with caffeine. The authors suggested that XPV heterozygotes can be identified by UV sensitivity in the presence of nontoxic caffeine.

checks.explanation: The two families and two patients are stated, but the abstract never explicitly calls the families Japanese. This is only implied by the Japanese control group.

paragraphs.text: Masutani et al. (1999) had used an improved cell-free assay to isolate a DNA polymerase from HeLa cells that, in XP-V cell extracts, continued replication on damaged DNA by bypassing UV-induced thymine dimers. They showed that this polymerase is a human homolog of yeast Rad30 (DNA polymerase eta), a member of a family of damage-bypass replication proteins that also includes E. coli UmuC and DinB and yeast Rev1. Masutani et al. (1999) found mutations in the DNA polymerase eta gene (POLH) in all XP-V cells they examined. Recombinant human DNA polymerase eta corrected the inability of XP-V cell extracts to replicate damaged DNA by bypassing thymine dimers. The authors concluded that DNA polymerase eta could be the XPV gene product.

Of the 8 mutations identified, 7 were predicted to result in a severely truncated hRad30 protein. The authors concluded that defects in hRAD30 cause XP-V.

paragraphs.text: Cleaver et al. (1980) irradiated XP variant and pigmented xerodermoid cells with UV light and measured unscheduled DNA synthesis, strand breakage during repair, chain growth during semiconservative replication with or without caffeine, and recovery of DNA replication. They concluded that the common defect appeared to be loss of a gene product that allows normal cells to replicate DNA without interruption at UV-induced pyrimidine dimers, so that replication forks were blocked more often and at lower doses in XP variant cells. They suggested that this defect correlated with the high levels of actinic carcinogenesis in these patients.

checks.evidence_quote: XP and pigmented xerodermoid cell cultures were irradiated with ultraviolet light and unscheduled DNA synthesis, strand breakage during repair, chain growth during semiconservative DNA replication with or without caffeine, and the recovery of DNA replication were determined.

paragraphs.text: Wang et al. (1991) transfected an XP variant cell line with a supF shuttle vector plasmid irradiated with UV at 254 nm. Mutant frequency rose linearly with dose, with a slope 5 times steeper than previously seen in normal cells. In 52 of 53 independent mutants the change was a base substitution, and 62 of 64 substitutions involved a dipyrimidine. A.T base pairs were involved in 28% of mutations in XP variant cells versus 11% in normal cells, mostly at position 136. The authors suggested that XP variant cells are less likely than normal cells to incorporate dAMP opposite photoproducts, which could account for their UV hypermutability.

checks.claim: Wang et al. (1991) found that mutant frequency in the XP variant cell line rose linearly with UV dose, with a slope 5 times steeper than previously seen in normal cells.

paragraphs.text: Using DNA combing, Despras et al. (2010) showed that the translesion synthesis defect in UV-irradiated XP-V cells, which lack DNA polymerase eta, caused a strong reduction in the number of active replication forks and a high proportion of stalled forks, in contrast to budding yeast. Extensive regions of single-strand DNA formed during replication, and the ATR/Chk1 pathway was overactivated after low UVC doses. Adding a low concentration of caffeine after irradiation lowered Chk1 activation and abolished DNA synthesis in XP-V cells. The Chk1 inhibitor UCN-01 worsened the replication defect in XP-V cells by increasing fork stalling and, like caffeine, made XP-V cells more sensitive to UVC. The authors concluded that pol eta acts at stalled forks to restart them, and that in its absence Chk1 becomes essential for replication to resume by alternative pathways through fork stabilization.

checks.evidence_quote: Using DNA combing, we showed that translesion synthesis defect leads to a strong reduction in the number of active replication forks
checks.explanation: The abstract says DNA combing was used. It also says pol eta is deficient in XP-V: "DNA polymerase eta (poleta) ... is deficient in cancer-prone xeroderma pigmentosum variant (XP-V) syndrome."

checks.claim: Despras et al. (2010) showed that the translesion synthesis defect in UV-irradiated XP-V cells caused a strong reduction in the number of active replication forks and a high proportion of stalled forks, in contrast to budding yeast.
checks.evidence_quote: translesion synthesis defect leads to a strong reduction in the number of active replication forks and a high proportion of stalled forks in human cells, which contrasts with budding yeast.

checks.claim: Despras et al. (2010) found that adding a low concentration of caffeine after irradiation lowered Chk1 activation and abolished DNA synthesis in XP-V cells.
checks.evidence_quote: Addition of a low concentration of caffeine post-irradiation, although inefficient to restore S-phase progression, significantly decreases Chk1 activation and abrogates DNA synthesis in XP-V cells.
checks.explanation: The abstract states this directly; the draft's "lowered" and "abolished" paraphrase "decreases" and "abrogates".

paragraphs.text: Itoh et al. (1996) described a simple autoradiographic method for diagnosing XP variant that measures 3 cellular markers after UV irradiation: unscheduled DNA synthesis (UDS), recovery of RNA synthesis, and recovery of replicative DNA synthesis. Patient fibroblasts were plated on coverslips alongside normal control cells, and grain counts on nuclei were compared. Among hereditary photosensitive disorders (XP, Cockayne syndrome, and UV-sensitive syndrome), only XP variant cells showed normal UDS and normal recovery of RNA synthesis but reduced recovery of replicative DNA synthesis (about 50% of control), and caffeine made this reduction greater. Because each of these disorders produces a different combination of the 3 markers, the method also gives a systematic basis for their diagnosis. Before this method, XP variant had been diagnosed using a postreplication repair assay together with clinical features.

checks.evidence_quote: an alternative simple method for the diagnosis of xeroderma pigmentosum variant that measures three cellular markers for DNA repair by autoradiography, unscheduled DNA synthesis, recovery of RNA synthesis, and recovery of replicative DNA synthesis after ultraviolet irradiation
checks.explanation: The abstract describes the same method and the same three markers.

checks.evidence_quote: Fibroblasts from a patient are plated on three coverslips parallel with normal cells (control).
checks.explanation: The comparison of grain counts on nuclei is stated in the next sentence of the abstract.

checks.evidence_quote: only xeroderma pigmentosum variant cells exhibit normal unscheduled DNA synthesis, normal recovery of RNA synthesis, but reduced recovery of replicative DNA synthesis (approximately 50% of that of control cells)
checks.explanation: The abstract states this among XP, Cockayne syndrome and UV-sensitive syndrome.

checks.evidence_quote: This reduction of DNA synthesis is enhanced in the presence of caffeine.
checks.explanation: "Enhanced" means caffeine made the reduction greater, as the claim says.

checks.claim: Because XP, Cockayne syndrome, and UV-sensitive syndrome each produce a different combination of the 3 markers, the method of Itoh et al. (1996) gives a systematic basis for their diagnosis.
checks.evidence_quote: Because each disorder yields a different combination of these three markers, this method also provides a systematic basis for the diagnosis of these diseases.
checks.explanation: The claim restates the abstract's conclusion.

checks.claim: Before the method of Itoh et al. (1996), XP variant had been diagnosed using a postreplication repair assay together with clinical features.
checks.evidence_quote: Patients with xeroderma pigmentosum variant have been diagnosed based on a post-replication repair assay using their cells together with their clinical manifestations.
checks.explanation: The abstract states that this was the previous way of diagnosing XP variant.

paragraphs.text: In a Japanese patient with XPV, Itoh et al.
